claims.text: This blog post covers cloud infrastructure trends for 2027 and beyond, including agentic infrastructure, hyperscaler AI spend, Kubernetes, IaC, DevSecOps, and platform engineering.
In 2027, AI agents are moving from writing code to operating infrastructure directly, with humans approving changes rather than authoring every one.
Microsoft's Azure business crossed $100 billion in trailing revenue.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion.
AWS's AI business and its custom-silicon business each passed a $25 billion annualized run rate.
This blog's 2026 edition predicted a cloud-first, AI-driven decade, and that prediction held up according to this post.
According to Gartner, by 2028 cloud-native platforms will serve as the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
Gartner forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027.
According to McKinsey & Company's "In search of cloud value" report, cloud value is driven by innovation, which is worth 5x more than cost savings.
According to McKinsey & Company's "In search of cloud value" report, high-performing organizations will see an EBITDA uplift of 20-30% by 2030.
According to McKinsey & Company's "In search of cloud value" report, Asia leads in projected cloud value, followed by the US and Europe.

According to McKinsey & Company's "In search of cloud value" report, high-ROI organizations excel by aligning cloud strategy with business priorities, building strong cloud foundations, and using modern operating models.
AWS posted its fastest revenue growth since 2021, at $42.2 billion in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year, accelerating from 28% growth the prior quarter.
AWS's AI business and its chips business, including custom Trainium and Graviton silicon, each exceeded a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate, growing triple-digit percentages year-over-year.

Microsoft Azure's full fiscal-year 2026 revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time in Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026 (ended June 30, 2026), with Azure revenue growing 43% year-over-year, up from 40% the prior quarter.
Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and CEO, said: "This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time."
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion, up from $106 billion a year earlier.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195-205 billion, up from an earlier $180-190 billion estimate that had itself already been raised twice this year.
Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39% year-over-year.

Oracle's remaining performance obligations reached $638 billion, up 363% year-over-year, on the strength of large-scale AI infrastructure contracts, including prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals now totaling $75 billion.
The hybrid cloud market will grow from $130B to $310-330B by 2030, according to ResearchAndMarkets.
87% of enterprises run workloads across multiple clouds, according to Mordor Intelligence.
Gartner predicts that 40% of enterprises will adopt hybrid compute architectures in mission-critical workflows by 2028, up from 8%.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers, 64% of respondents run on AWS, 55% on Google Cloud, and 45% on Azure, with most running more than one cloud.
claims.source_hint: Pulumi (2026 State of Agentic Infrastructure survey)

claims.text: According to Gartner, total worldwide AI spending, spanning software, hardware, and services, is forecast to reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC predicts that by 2027, half of enterprises will be using AI agents to redefine how humans and machines collaborate.
Pulumi Policies help teams detect misconfigurations, analyze usage patterns, and generate infrastructure updates through AI-driven optimization and insights.
Gartner predicts that by 2028, over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms to secure third-party AI service usage and protect custom-built AI applications.
Total spending on securing AI is predicted to reach roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.

At the Gartner Data & Analytics Summit in Sydney, Carlie Idoine, VP Analyst at Gartner, said: "[AI]... it doesn't deliver value on its own – AI needs to be tightly aligned with data, analytics, and governance to enable intelligent, adaptive decisions and actions across the organization."

According to Gartner, by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams as internal providers of reusable services, components, and tools for application delivery.
CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 28% of surveyed organizations already have a dedicated platform engineering team.
CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 35% of surveyed organizations are running a hybrid platform that combines existing developer platforms with specialized AI tooling.

Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said: "Cloud native platforms have reached a point where developers are not just experimenting but standardizing on CNCF projects that make software delivery reliable at scale. What's especially notable about this research is how organizations are extending those same platforms to support AI workloads, showing how cloud native is the base layer of powering the next era of applications."
Mid-size to large companies continue to invest in implementing platform engineering practices, with large tech companies as first adopters.
Gartner predicts that agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029.
Gartner predicts that human-in-the-loop requirements in IT operations workflows fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers, 82% of respondents agree that AI and agents will meaningfully change how they write infrastructure within 12 months.
claims.source_hint: Pulumi (2026 State of Agentic Infrastructure survey)

claims.text: Pulumi Neo is built around a loop of proposing infrastructure changes, running previews, and executing approved updates with policy guardrails in place.
According to Mordor Intelligence, the global Kubernetes market is valued at USD 3.13 billion in 2026 and is projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.
The CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among professional ML/AI developers at 41%.

The CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report finds 30% of backend developers now using Kubernetes directly, down from a peak of 36% in Q3 2023, a decline the report attributes to the technology's growing maturity.
Kubernetes is evolving in response to AI demands, a shift Pulumi covers in more depth in its comparison of Kubernetes IaC tools.
AI-powered coding assistants like GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, and others have moved from novelty to everyday tooling for a large share of enterprise software teams.
According to Gartner, by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use dedicated AI code assistants.
According to Gartner, 63% of organizations are currently piloting, deploying, or beginning to use AI code assistants.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is described by its maintainers as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
AWS shipped a general-availability MCP server for its Agent Toolkit.
Mirantis's Lens has released a built-in MCP server connecting AI coding assistants to Kubernetes.
Pulumi Agent Skills is a collection of infrastructure expertise packaged for use in AI coding assistants.

Pulumi Agent Skills teaches tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI to reason about Pulumi projects, reducing hallucination and improving outputs based on real infrastructure conventions and practices.

Pulumi's Remote MCP Server provides infrastructure access that, combined with Pulumi Neo, lets teams build secure, AI-driven workflows where assistants provide insights and Pulumi Neo safely executes actions with previews, policies, and orchestration.
Cloud infrastructure is entering its most transformative era since the rise of Kubernetes.
Modern IaC, unified governance, reusable components, and policy frameworks are all core capabilities of the Pulumi Cloud platform.
